South Australia was a British colony in southern Australia, founded in 1836 with its capital at Adelaide. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900, before it became a state of Australia in 1901.

It was planned as a colony of free settlers, with no convicts. Its founders followed the ideas of Edward Gibbon Wakefield, who wanted land sold at a set price and the money used to bring out labourers. It promised religious freedom, and German Lutherans arrived from 1838 and farmed the Adelaide Hills and the Barossa Valley. Copper mines at Kapunda and Burra in the 1840s saved its early finances, and wheat and wool followed.

  • In 1856 it adopted the secret ballot, in the same year as Victoria.
  • From 1863 to 1911 it also governed the Northern Territory.
  • In 1872 it finished the Overland Telegraph Line from Adelaide to Darwin, linking Australia to the world's cable network.
  • In 1894 women won the right to vote and to stand for parliament, among the first anywhere, a step in women's suffrage in Australia.

The colony was built on the lands of the Kaurna, the Ngarrindjeri and many other peoples.
sum: South Australia was a British colony in southern Australia, founded in 1836 with its capital at Adelaide. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900, before it became a state of Australia in 1901.
